name: inprocess-obi-apb-two-rate-timers-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU at its pinned 50 MHz declaration reaches two PULP APB3 timers whose declared composition rates are 25 MHz and 10 MHz in the same session. The entry normalizes 50/25 = 2 and 50/10 = 5 into per-model half-period dividers, the host drives each target's own low-first clock at its declared rate and samples each target's APB3 trace once per that target's own cycle, and the saved plan/summary state the ratio and the measured per-model cycles. No DMA and no IRQ behavior is declared, so F5/F6 are refused by name.
notes: The two target profiles are declared composition variants: same pinned PULP apb_timer RTL/source revision as configs/peripherals/pulp_timer, only the declared frequency_hz differs (25000000 and 10000000).  The pinned profile keeps its own 50000000 Hz declaration and is not edited; assume_single_clock is deliberately absent so the per-model divider is the only admitted schedule.

The reference CPU is the 50 MHz Ibex model: 50/25 = 2 and 50/10 = 5 are whole half-period ratios, so each target keeps the low-first phase its own clock schedule declares and its first rising edge is at its own half period.  A ratio that is not a whole divisor (for example 30 Hz beside 50 Hz) is refused by name, as is a model faster than the reference CPU.

The host samples each target's APB3 trace once per that target's own cycle: a 25 MHz target is sampled on one tick in two and a 10 MHz target on one in five.  The case lines keep their historical bytes; a separate 'clockcase' line per case and the summary's clock_* fields state the per-model rising-edge counts, so the ratio is measured rather than asserted.
No behavior file and no DMA profile are declared: this scenario claims only F1-F4, and F5/F6 stay named refusals (unsupported-f5:target-irq-semantics:apb3:... and unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB3).
